name: microduck
one_liner: Open-source plans and software brains for a tiny two-legged walking robot the size of a toy duck, controlled by AI trained in simulation.
buyer: A STEM teacher, university robotics lab, or hobbyist robotics club that wants an affordable, real physical robot to teach reinforcement learning and walking-robot control hands-on.
business_use_cases: A robotics educator buys kits and runs a paid after-school or university workshop teaching students to train and deploy walking-robot AI policies.
A university lab uses Microduck as a cheap, reproducible research platform for sim-to-real robotics experiments instead of building custom hardware.
A robotics YouTuber builds a content series around assembling, training, and competing Microducks, monetizing through sponsorships and kit affiliate links.

money_ideas.idea: Run paid robotics workshops or summer camps using Microduck kits as the hands-on hardware.
Sell add-on hardware (custom shells, sensors) or pre-trained specialty walking policies to existing Microduck owners.

steal_this: If you already have the hardware, record a short 'teach your robot to walk' tutorial series and sell it as a paid mini-course to hobbyists buying the kit.
